item.title: Tampa Bay Lightning visit Buffalo Sabres with both goalies struggling to stop pucks this season
item.description: Andrei Vasilevskiy and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen both rank outside starter-level quality in save percentage, setting up a high-scoring NHL clash.
item.content:encoded:
It has been a while since I put out an NHL play, and I'd like to get a bit more consistent with playing NHL games. There isn't a huge slate of games tonight, but there are certainly some intriguing ones. Hockey is the one sport that I don't follow quite as much, but I've made concerted efforts over the years to try to follow the regular season closer. It seems like this year has had more big names with trade requests (earlier) too, and has been a pretty exciting early season. Tonight, the Lightning and Sabres battle in one of the better games of the night.

The Tampa Bay Lightning are off to a great start with an 11-4-2 record. All four of their losses, though, have been on the road. They are just 3-4-2 for the season on the road. Their offense has looked great this season with a 3.71 goals-per-game average, but they are allowing 3.06 goals per game as well. Their defense probably needs to improve in terms of giving up good looks. They are allowing just 24.7 shots per game, but if they are giving up three goals per game, either the shots are good ones, or the goalie play is lacking.

Over the past five games, the Lightning have won three games and lost the other two, with one in a shootout. Andrei Vasilevskiy is likely to be in the net tonight. He is 8-4-1 for the season and is allowing 2.85 goals per game, which is 24th in the nation. He only has an .883 save percentage, which puts him at 33rd in the league. As a starting goalie, that wouldn't even rank him as a top option in the league. He has been in the net for all four of the road losses this season as well.

NHL'S REIGNING MVP NIKITA KUCHEROV REPORTEDLY ASKS LIGHTNING FOR TRADE IN STUNNING MOVE

The Buffalo Sabres are not exactly great to start the season, but they aren't playing poorly either. For the season, Buffalo is 8-6-3, and only 4-5-0 for the year on their home ice. Their offense has been fine, but not great. The Sabres are scoring just under three goals per game, and they allow 3.29 goals per game. The Sabres are allowing about the same number of shots per game to opponents as they are taking. The Sabres are playing decent enough hockey lately, but they are 1-2 at home in their current home streak.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Tonight, they are likely to send the owner of my favorite name in hockey, Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen, into the net. The 27-year-old Finniard hasn't been that impressive this season. Luukkonen is allowing 3.27 goals per game, which is 38th in the league. He also has an .878 save percentage this season, putting him at 48th in the league. Just like Vasilevskiy, this makes Luukkonen not even starter-level quality. He has been better at home this season than on the road. In his home games, he is only allowing 2.88 goals per game.

Neither of the defenses look that good this season, and the goalies are letting a lot of pucks past them. On offense, they are both averaging three goals. Neither has been scoring a ton in recent games, though. Tampa has gone over 6.5 goals in three of the past five games. Buffalo has had seven or more goals in a game in just two of the past five games. I do think this is one that finds at least seven goals between the two teams. Give me the over.

item.title: Horny bull elk keeps attacking cars, forces Missouri wildlife park to close indefinitely
item.description: Lone Elk Park near St. Louis closed indefinitely after a young bull elk in his first mating season began ramming visitors' cars with his antlers.
item.content:encoded:
A wildlife park in Missouri has been forced to close indefinitely because one particularly aggressive bull elk won't stop attacking visitors' cars.

Lone Elk Park, located just outside St. Louis, closed Monday after officials decided the animal had become too much of a safety risk. Apparently, the problem is that he's young, he's horny, and he's new to this whole being-in-charge thing.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

According to St. Louis Public Radio, the bull recently replaced his own father as the dominant male in the herd. This is his first mating season running the show, and he's not exactly handling his newfound responsibilities gracefully.

"We have a younger, more inexperienced herd bull this year," Eric Johnson, acting director of St. Louis County Parks and Recreation, said. "It's his first year, and he's acting a little bit like a teenager."

One visitor, Theresa Hammer, learned that the hard way.

Hammer told St. Louis Public Radio she was sitting in her Ford Fusion last week when the bull approached her vehicle. She looked away briefly, and when she looked back, he was ramming his antlers into the front of her car.

"I looked back up, and he hit the front of my car with his horns," she said. "He scratched up the whole side of my car, my hood and put a big dent in the rear quarter panel."

Despite the damage, Hammer said she doesn't blame the elk. After all, she's the one driving through his home.

Lone Elk Park is a 546-acre drive-through wildlife park where visitors can observe elk, bison and other animals from their vehicles. Officials had posted warnings about keeping a safe distance from the elk, but visitors weren't always following them.

And with the bull becoming increasingly aggressive, the county decided it was safer to close the park until he settles down.

BULL ELK IN COLORADO NICKNAMED 'SMASH' IS CHASING OFF TRUCKS AND GOLF CARTS

For what it's worth, this kind of behavior isn't unusual during the elk rut, which is the annual breeding season. Bull elk experience a surge in testosterone and become more territorial as they compete for females. That can make them particularly dangerous to people who get too close.

But even by elk standards, this guy is apparently a handful.

Johnson, who has worked for the parks department for 32 years, said it's been roughly a decade since they've dealt with a bull quite this worked up.

"Some of [the bulls] have it figured out and they calmly go about their business, and sometimes it's like this," he said.

Officials haven't announced a reopening date, but they're monitoring the bull's behavior daily and hope to reopen the park within the next several days.

So, for now, an entire wildlife park is closed because one young elk can't get his hormones under control.

Nature is beautiful.

item.title: Russian Ambassador to US Alexander Darchiev dies suddenly at 66
item.description: Russia's ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev, 66, had been appointed by Putin to lead a rapprochement with the Trump administration.
item.content:encoded:
Russia's Ambassador to the United States Alexander Darchiev, 66, died suddenly Wednesday, the Russian Foreign Ministry announced.

"The leadership and staff of the Russian Foreign Ministry report with deep sorrow that on Nov. 11, at the age of 66, the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Russian Federation to the United States of America, Alexander Nikitich Darchiev, passed away suddenly," Russia's statement, as translated to English, said. "A distinguished diplomat, experienced leader, kind colleague, and mentor has departed this life. A consummate professional and brilliant Americanist, A.N. Darchiev served on one of the most critical and demanding fronts of Russian foreign policy."

"We express our deepest and most sincere condolences to the family and loved ones of Alexander Nikitich Darchiev," the statement added. "The cherished memory of our untimely departed colleague will forever remain in our hearts."

MELANIA TRUMP HAILS OLESHKY CEASEFIRE AS POTENTIAL ‘SPARK’ FOR PROGRESS AMID UKRAINE-RUSSIA WAR

Russia's Vladimir Putin appointed Darchiev, a veteran diplomat known in the past for his public denunciations of the West, as ambassador to Washington in March 2025 to lead a rapprochement with the Trump administration that has rattled Ukraine, the European Union and NATO.

His death comes less than a week after a White House news conference hailing a temporary ceasefire in Ukrainian territory occupied by Russia.

First lady Melania Trump and envoys from both Russia and Ukraine hailed the ceasefire in the Oleshky region.

"We have chosen humanity over war," the first lady said. "Undeniably, the lives of innocent people must transcend the division of war. I hope Oleshky inspires greater peace. Every significant transformation begins with a small spark."

KUSHNER ENTERS UKRAINE PEACE TALKS AS TRUMP EYES SECURING SAFEGUARDS AGAINST ANOTHER RUSSIAN INVASION

Shortly after being tapped as ambassador, Darchiev met with Trump administration officials and delivered a message of hope for peace.

"Russia and the United States are destined, as great powers, to have non-confrontational peaceful existence," Darchiev said during a June 10, 2025, Russia Day reception at the Russian Embassy in Washington after delivering his credentials to the White House, adding, "our discussion was very constructive."

Before taking the helm of the Russian Embassy in Washington, Darchiev played a role as the Kremlin’s point man for high-stakes bilateral negotiations, most notably during the delicate discussions that led to prisoner swaps involving imprisoned arms dealer Viktor Bout and detained Americans Brittney Griner and Paul Whelan.

EVAN GERSHKOVICH DETAILS RUSSIAN ARREST, REVEALS MOMENT THAT NEARLY BROKE HIM DURING WRONGFUL DETENTION

In August 2022, while serving as the director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s North American Department, Darchiev provided the first on-the-record Russian confirmation that Moscow and Washington were actively discussing those situations.

"This quite sensitive issue of the swap of convicted Russian and U.S. citizens is being pursued along the channels designated by our presidents," Darchiev told the Russian state news agency TASS. "The individuals are, indeed, being discussed. The Russian side has long been seeking the release of Viktor Bout. The negotiations are bearing fruit."

His comments marked a breakthrough moment in months of backchannel diplomacy, which ultimately culminated in December 2022 when the U.S. and Russia completed a one-for-one swap of Griner for Bout at an airport in Abu Dhabi.

The Associated Press and Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Teen charged with murder in fatal shooting of 15-year-old NYC student Javits Frimpong
item.description: A 17-year-old faces a murder charge in the New York City shooting of Javits Frimpong, a 15-year-old Ghanaian immigrant killed walking to school.
item.content:encoded:
A 17-year-old boy has been arrested after a teenager was fatally shot while walking to school in New York City last month, police announced Wednesday.

The teen suspect, who has not been publicly identified, faces a murder charge in the Oct. 29 death of 15-year-old Javits Frimpong, according to the New York City Police Department (NYPD).

"The NYPD will be relentless in our efforts to get dangerous people out of our communities, especially when it involves the murder of a 15-year-old boy," the department wrote in a post on X.

Javits, a Ghanaian immigrant, was fatally shot in the stomach in the Bronx. His father believes the killing may be linked to ongoing bullying his son experienced at school.

Just two days before the tragedy, the school’s principal had called Thomas Frimpong to report that his son was being targeted and that two students had been suspended as a result.

The tragic killing sparked local protests and urgent calls from community members to end youth violence and bullying.

Last week, NYPD Chief of Detectives Joseph Kenny noted that investigators were exploring multiple angles.

"The alleged bullying is one aspect that we’re looking at, as well as some others," Kenny told the New York Post.

"All three gave chase," Kenny added. "And these cowards shot him in the back. If their intention was to rob him, he dropped his backpack."

PARENTS IN BRONX NEIGHBORHOOD PLEAD FOR NYPD GUARD AS MAMDANI CUTS COPS, HALTS HIRES: 'HORRIBLE SITUATION'

"As of right now, all indications are that he was trying to live the American dream," the chief said. "He was trying to get ahead by going to school. We have nothing in our investigation to indicate he was involved in any gang activity. Seems like he was just a very good kid."

The tragedy also prompted federal intervention to support the grieving family. President Donald Trump agreed to grant Javits’ mother an emergency visa so she could travel to the United States from Ghana to lay her son to rest.

"The murder of a child is a pain no parent should have to endure, let alone from thousands of miles away," New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani wrote in a Nov. 2 post on X. 

"Javits Frimpong’s mother deserves to say goodbye to her son in person. I just got off the phone with President Trump, and he has agreed to grant her visa immediately."

item.title: Biden ripped for ‘totally delusional’ claim about debate that preceded his 2024 exit
item.description: Joe Biden tells People Magazine his disastrous June 2024 presidential debate against Trump was "not very consequential," drawing sharp criticism.
item.content:encoded:
Former President Joe Biden is facing sharp backlash after dismissing his disastrous 2024 debate performance against President Donald Trump as "not very consequential" — despite dropping out of the presidential race just 24 days later.

When asked about what his "perspective" on the June 27, 2024 debate is now in an interview with People Magazine released Wednesday, Biden suggested he felt his debate performance was inconsequential.

"Look, I don’t know anybody who hasn’t made a mistake in a debate," Biden told People Magazine. "To me, it was not very consequential. First of all, I thought there’d be another debate, which there wasn’t."

JILL BIDEN SAYS SHE THOUGHT JOE WAS HAVING A STROKE DURING HIS DISASTROUS 2024 DEBATE PERFORMANCE

"But notwithstanding the fact that there wasn’t another debate, it didn’t disturb me because it wasn’t consequential," he added.

Biden's comments drew swift criticism on social media on Wednesday.

SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS AFTER JILL BIDEN REVEALS SHE WAS 'FRIGHTENED' WATCHING JOE'S DISASTROUS DEBATE

"Joe Biden now claims his 2024 presidential debate against President Trump, which forced him to drop out of the race, was not very consequential," former Trump campaign operative Steve Cortes wrote Wednesday in an X post.

"Just 24 days after the 'not very consequential' presidential debate, Joe Biden ended his campaign for President," Cortes added.

Conservative commentator Steve Guest wrote on X that Biden "is TOTALLY delusional."

Meanwhile, former National Republican Senatorial Committee senior adviser Matt Whitlock asserted in a Wednesday post on X that it was actually "the most consequential" presidential debate of all time.

"It was without question the most consequential Presidential debate in history - he [Biden] likely would have stayed the nominee without it," Whitlock said. "But I’m definitely excited for the other hot takes in the book now."

"It was the most lopsided debate in history. C’mon, man!" Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis quipped.

During the presidential debate, Biden stumbled over his words, paused for long periods of time and displayed confused facial expressions.

The Office of Joe and Jill Biden did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

"Biden subsequently dropped out of the presidential race on July 21, 2024, just a few weeks after the debate, amid mounting pressure from Democratic allies to end his re-election bid.

Former first lady Jill Biden notably claimed in a CBS News Sunday Morning interview clip released in May 2026 that she thought her husband was having a stroke on stage during the debate.

Trump's White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

Additionally, Biden said Sunday that he plans to scale back public appearances promoting his new presidential memoir, "Promise Me, America," due to his cancer battle.

"My presidential memoir, PROMISE ME, AMERICA, is coming out on November 17th. I hope you'll read it. It covers my years as President. The challenges we faced, the decisions I made, and why I made them. It's about who we are as a nation," Biden said in an X post. "What we stand for. And America's role in the world."

"While writing the book, I was diagnosed with cancer, a disease known all too well to millions of Americans and their families," the former president added. "My doctors continue to be encouraged by how I've responded to treatment. And the prayers and kind words and well wishes from so many of you have meant more to me and Jill and our family than you can ever know. Some days are better than others. It hasn't stopped me. But sometimes it slows me down."

item.title: Jim Caviezel says a surreal encounter with Jesus convinced him to star in 'The Passion of the Christ'
item.description: Jim Caviezel says he told Jesus "get somebody else" before a heartbreaking response convinced him to accept "The Passion of the Christ" role.
item.content:encoded:
Actor Jim Caviezel said he nearly turned down the role of Jesus in "The Passion of the Christ," but an encounter he described as a visit from Jesus convinced him to reconsider.

"About 5 something in the morning, this presence came over me, and I know it was him," Caviezel, 58, told Sean Hannity on his "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast.

"I was awake, but my eyes were closed, and he was sitting Indian style on the foot of my bed, and he said, 'It is not a requirement of you as a Catholic… to play this role.' And I said, 'Good, I won't. Get somebody else.'"

STEPHEN BALDWIN ON CHOOSING BORN-AGAIN CHRISTIANITY OVER HOLLYWOOD AFTER A LIFE-CHANGING ENCOUNTER WITH GOD

Caviezel said the figure appeared sad after he refused, leading to an exchange that prompted him to reconsider.

"I said, 'Get somebody else,' and his countenance changed, and then he says, 'I don't have anybody else,'" Caviezel recalled.

When Caviezel questioned why he had been chosen, he said the figure responded that others would not ask the same question of him. After some exchange, Caviezel was convinced the role was his to play.

"Immediately, I was like, OK, this is part of the plan. I'm in," he said.

MEL GIBSON REVEALS ‘THE PASSION OF THE CHRIST’S’ MOST SURPRISING LEGACY IN NEW RAYMOND ARROYO INTERVIEW

Caviezel is best known for his performance as Christ in the Mel Gibson-directed 2004 film "The Passion of the Christ," which follows the final hours of Jesus' life, including his crucifixion.

The role became a defining performance of his career, but Caviezel said filming took a severe physical toll.

During production, Caviezel said he injured his shoulder, suffered hypothermia and was struck by lightning while filming a scene.

"It nearly killed me," Caviezel recalled of the hypothermia.

"When you watch the end of the movie, I'm blue for a reason. My body's blue. There's no fake stuff there."

The podcast episode comes as the actor returns to the big screen in the action thriller "Ghost Soldier" and prepares for the release of "Zero A.D.: The Birth of Christ," in which he plays King Herod.

During his conversation with Hannity, Caviezel also discussed what he described as a near-death experience, the lasting impact of his work with Mel Gibson and the spiritual battles he believes have shaped his life and career.

Viewers and listeners can find the Fox News host's full conversation with Caviezel on the "Hang Out with Sean Hannity" podcast, available on YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts and iHeartRadio.

item.title: GOP congressman-elect makes unusual Trump request, ejects reporter during profanity-laced victory speech
item.description: Anthony Constantino kicked a reporter out of the room and called on Trump to pardon Diddy during his profanity-laden congressional victory speech.
item.content:encoded:
Anthony Constantino, a former boxer and the CEO of the printing company Sticker Mule, delivered a profanity-laden victory speech after his election to New York’s 21st Congressional District, kicking a reporter out of the room and calling on President Donald Trump to pardon Sean "Diddy" Combs.

"I think President Trump should consider freeing Diddy," Constantino said, referring to the incarcerated producer.

"A historic New Yorker that did great things for New York State. I think we should consider it."

Constantino’s brazen speech contrasts sharply with the demeanor of the district’s outgoing incumbent, Rep. Elise Stefanik, R-N.Y., the former No. 3 Republican in the House of Representatives. It also raises questions about whether Constantino earnestly hopes to see the administration pardon Combs, who was convicted of prostitution across state lines.

DIDDY'S FEDERAL PRISON RELEASE DELAYED WEEKS AFTER REPORTED SOLITARY CONFINEMENT STINT

"Where’s my lawyer at? I have a very good lawyer. Listen, I’m fighting for New York. I want to bring excitement back to New York. I want to bring jobs back to New York," Constantino said moments before his request.

During his 31-minute speech, Constantino spoke about political allies, enemies, the media, power struggles and his vision for the country. He even had a rapper friend perform a freestyle tribute to his congressional election.

At points, Constantino adopted an openly combative tone — especially with respect to members of the press.

"Listen to me, scumbags. Telling people the truth is the right thing to do. I had to listen to you a--holes say ‘dairy farmer Blake Gendebien,’" Constantino said, referring to news coverage of his Democratic challenger.

"He’s not a dairy farmer; his parents were dairy farmers … but you wouldn’t say that because you’re a bunch of f---ing a--holes," he added.

At one point, Constantino singled out a pair of reporters in the crowd.

"Look at that a--hole right there. Him. Look at that guy. Take a picture of him … and Kay Lisa, another f---ing a--hole."

Constantino then ordered one of the reporters removed from the room, describing him as an "angry motherf---er."

ANTIFA SUPPORTER CHARGED WITH STEALING GOP CAMPAIGN SIGNS IN NY RACE TO REPLACE STEFANIK

"Actually, do me a favor. This guy is so — he’s looking at me. Kick him out. Just kick him out. Get him out of here. You’re just a rude person. If you want to be tough on me, get out. Go right now. I’m not playing games with you. You deleted two of my interviews … bye bye," Constantino said.

Stefanik, a former GOP conference chair and Trump’s first pick to become U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, was considered by many a rising star within the Republican Party.

Although Stefanik began the confirmation process for the nomination, Trump ultimately rescinded his pick, calling on Stefanik to remain in the House, where Republicans held a razor-thin majority. A few months later, Stefanik announced that she would not pursue reelection or a bid for governor, citing a desire to focus on her family and avoid a primary contest.

Notably, Stefanik endorsed Constantino after the GOP primary for New York’s 21st Congressional District.

"In the coming months, I know Anthony will continue to work hard to earn your support. He will put the people first and will be a strong representative in Washington for the incredible hardworking families in our great district," Stefanik said in a post to social media.

Constantino also secured backing from President Donald Trump.

Constantino made headlines in 2024 when he put up a giant 100-foot "VOTE FOR TRUMP" sign atop his company building.

City officials, including Democratic Mayor Michael Cinquanti, argued the sign violated code because it "presents a dangerous distraction and impacts traffic flow," especially at night when it is illuminated.

After a legal battle, courts ruled that Constantino had a right to keep the sign in place, a decision he called an "epic win for free speech."

JOHN RICH SAYS KATHY HOCHUL IS ‘RUNNING OVER’ NY FARMERS WITH RENEWABLE ENERGY AGENDA

Last Tuesday, Constantino narrowly won his race in a 50.9% to 48.8% victory over Gendebien.

During his campaign, Constantino stressed his alignment with Trump, highlighting his record as a business owner, promised to bring reliable cell phone service to northern New York and reduce utility costs, according to his website.

Having secured his congressional race, Constantino will be sworn into office on Jan. 3, 2027, alongside the rest of the 120th Congress.

item.title: Iranian boxer on death row wins human rights award as athletes push to save his life
item.description: Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani faces execution in Iran after 2019 protest arrests. Athletes and the World Boxing Council have rallied to save him.
item.content:encoded:
An Iranian boxing champion on death row has won an international human rights award, bringing renewed attention to his case after prominent athletes urged Iran to spare his life.

Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani was named the 2026 Magnitsky Award winner for Outstanding Human Rights Activist, according to the award organizers. The honor is scheduled to be presented on his behalf Thursday in London, according to the National Council of Resistance of Iran, an opposition coalition.

British lawmaker Bob Blackman, chair of the British Committee for Iran Freedom, is listed as the award’s presenter.

Vafaei Sani, a boxer and coach from Mashhad, was arrested in 2020 following the November 2019 anti-government protests. Authorities accused him of supporting the opposition People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran, also known as the PMOI or MEK, according to the NCRI.

KEITH KELLOGG TELLS IRANIAN DISSIDENTS THE 'WINDOW IS OPEN' TO FORCE REGIME CHANGE IN TEHRAN

His prosecution involved allegations of arson and destruction of public property under the capital charge of "corruption on earth," according to IranWire. Rights advocates have condemned the proceedings as unfair.

The award organizers describe his case as a "symbol of the persecution of peaceful dissent" in Iran. They say he has endured physical and psychological torture, lengthy solitary confinement and repeated threats of execution.

Iran’s Supreme Court twice overturned his death sentence before a Revolutionary Court sentenced him to death again in September 2024. The Supreme Court upheld that third sentence in October 2025, according to the organizers and the Sport & Rights Alliance.

However, his lawyer, Babak Paknia, announced a stay of execution in December 2025, IranWire reported. That order paused the execution without overturning his conviction. IranWire reported last month that Human Rights for Sports continued to list him among athletes facing capital punishment.

IRANIAN AND ISRAELI ATHLETES REACT TO MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING TO END US-IRAN WAR

His case has drawn support from some of the most recognizable names in sports.

Tennis great Martina Navratilova, former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines, British Olympic swimming medalist Sharron Davies and three-time Olympic swimming gold medalist Nancy Hogshead signed a November 2025 appeal calling for international intervention.

Other signatories included former U.S. Olympic cyclist Inga Thompson and former Australian national soccer team captain Craig Foster.

"The world must not stand by while Iran silences its champions," the athletes’ statement said.

The World Boxing Council joined the calls to save Vafaei Sani in November 2025, urging the United Nations, International Olympic Committee and other sporting bodies to intervene.

IRAN HANGS 2 PROTESTERS IN PUBLIC, CROWD CRIES 'DISHONORABLE' AS SECURITY FIRES TEAR GAS

"From the WBC, we call on the Iranian authorities to reconsider and annul the death sentence against Mohammad Javad Vafaei Sani," WBC President Mauricio Sulaimán said.

The Sport & Rights Alliance separately raised his case with the IOC, arguing that its commitments to human rights and athlete protection required action. The alliance also cited Amnesty International’s objections that the charge of "corruption on earth" fails international standards requiring clear, legally defined offenses.

Amnesty included Vafaei Sani among people at risk of execution in a May 2026 urgent action concerning Iranian protesters and dissidents.

The international solidarity campaign extended beyond sports last month. Leopoldo Maldonado, the U.N. special rapporteur on freedom of opinion and expression, announced a 24-hour hunger strike in support of Iranian political prisoners, according to posts reproduced by Iran Freedom, an advocacy outlet. He highlighted Vafaei Sani among prisoners facing death sentences.

The Magnitsky Awards began in 2015 and recognize journalists, politicians and activists working to defend human rights. They are named for Sergei Magnitsky, who died in Russian custody after exposing government corruption.

Previous recipients include the late Sen. John McCain, journalist Maria Ressa and Russian opposition figure Boris Nemtsov, according to the organizers.

item.title: Top Dem on committee fires back after White House counsel warns against overreach amid investigation threats
item.description: White House counsel Will Scharf warns House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Rep. Robert Garcia against overreaching congressional authority.
item.content:encoded:
Counsel to the president William Scharf, in a letter to House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., warned against Democrats running afoul of their allotted powers pertaining to investigations and subpoenas.

But Garcia — who is poised to chair the committee next year when Democrats gain the House majority — fired back, asserting that President Donald Trump's administration is weaponizing the government.

"I write to remind you of the foundational limits that the Constitution imposes on congressional investigations and subpoenas, which you and members of the new Congress have evinced a clear intent to transgress," Scharf wrote in part of the letter.

'LAWYER UP': DEMS IMMEDIATELY PUT TRUMP ON NOTICE AMID REPUBLICANS' MIDTERM BLOODBATH

Republicans suffered a drubbing during the 2026 midterms and will consequently be the minority in both chambers of Congress next year.

In a statement on Election Day last week, Garcia warned, "Lawyer up."

Rep. Emily Randall, D-Wash., who is also on the committee, declared in a post last week on the social media platform Bluesky, "We’re going to be passing out subpoenas like candy."

In his letter, Scharf asserted, "We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government. Recent public statements underscore these concerns. You and your congressional colleagues have asserted that they will issue subpoenas to harass, threaten, and deter dedicated members of the Administration from further service."

"Compulsory process is a power Congress has for oversight functions, and only for oversight functions. Abusive threats and public statements about the indiscriminate issuance of subpoenas, along with threats directed at prospective targets within the Administration make it abundantly clear that any forthcoming investigative processes will be deployed to harass and aggrandize, rather than to advance any legitimate legislative end," Scharf's letter stated.

"Beyond being inconsistent with the clear, well-recognized constitutional limitations on your investigative functions, threats to executive branch officials designed to deter them from public service, or process designed merely to abuse or instill fear in the recipient may cross the line into blatant criminality," the letter continued. "And issuing unlawful subpoenas with the intention of depriving citizens of their constitutional rights and privileges may warrant further investigation."

DEMS PIVOT FROM 'AFFORDABILITY' PITCH TO DHS PROBE THREATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

Responding to the letter, Garcia suggested in a statement that the president is hiding something from the public.

"It appears Donald Trump has something to hide. Let’s be clear: Congress' authority comes from Article I of the Constitution, not from the permission of the White House. Congress has wide latitude to conduct investigations and oversight, an authority inherent in the power to legislate," Garcia said in his statement.

"The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse. The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers," Garcia stated.

TRUMP ORDERS DOJ PROBE INTO DEMOCRATS OVER ALLEGED THREATS AGAINST ADMINISTRATION OFFICIALS

The White House did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment on Wednesday.

item.title: Trump defends Iran war during Veterans Day address, says he is making the world 'safer'
item.description: Trump told veterans at Arlington National Cemetery that the Iran conflict will end soon, vowing "total victory" in his Veterans Day address.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump defended the war in Iran and said it will be over "soon" during his Veterans Day address on Wednesday.

Trump made the statement while speaking to a crowd of veterans and their families at Arlington National Cemetery. He highlighted the 1983 Iran-backed bombing of the U.S. Marine Corps barracks in Beirut and argued that Iran has been at war with the U.S. for decades.

"America did not start a war with Iran. Iran has been waging war on America since 1979. They should have been taken care of a long time ago," Trump said.

RUBIO'S DEFENSE OF TRUMP'S IRAN WAR DRAWS SHARP CONTRAST WITH VANCE'S MIDTERM BLAME

"And it was just about time somebody fought back. All of us fought back. We fought back, and we fought back. We won. Now the question is when we want to end. We must have a total victory. Not a 93% victory. It's going to be total," he continued.

Trump noted that of the roughly seven months of conflict, "only a few weeks were active fighting," but he acknowledged the casualties America sustained.

"We lost 18 beautiful souls," Trump said. "When this conflict is over, and it will be soon, the entire world will be much safer, a better place, more peaceful place and a place without the kind of danger that we had to suffer."

TRUMP WARNS IRAN FIGHTING ISN'T OVER AS HE VOWS US WILL 'WIN' AS TALKS FADE

Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio have shied away from plans to re-escalate the conflict with Iran following the midterm elections.

Administration officials have instead pointed to economic and diplomatic solutions to the conflict.

IRAN’S DEEPEST WEAKNESS IS GETTING EXPOSED THROUGH AMERICA’S MAXIMUM PRESSURE CAMPAIGN

"We don't need to conduct military strikes if we're achieving the same objective through economic means and economic pressure," Rubio told reporters on Tuesday.

He rejected the suggestion that the U.S. and Iran were at a stalemate, arguing that sanctions, the naval blockade and other measures were steadily weakening Tehran.

"They’re bleeding. They’re bleeding economically," Rubio said. "It is an increased pressure on Iran that continues to grow every day."

Fox News' Morgan Phillips contributed to this report.

item.title: Victor Wembanyama and the 9-2 Spurs look to continue routing opponents against the Bulls
item.description: Victor Wembanyama's 9-2 Spurs have been perfect on the road and won four of five games by 22-plus points heading into their matchup with Chicago.
item.content:encoded:
I've lost two NBA games in a row, and they were losers in two very different fashions. Two nights ago, I lost by a hook after two free throws were missed in the final few seconds of the game. Last night, I was just wrong. I picked the 76ers to win the game, and the Celtics went scorched earth on Philadelphia. The 76ers barely even decided to show up last night, and they completely forgot to guard Paul George. I prefer to lose like that as opposed to the first night. Tonight, the Spurs take on the Bulls, and I'm looking to stop the losing skid at two games.

Coming into the season, the San Antonio Spurs' biggest question was how they would respond to losing the NBA Championship. Only 15% of the way into the new campaign, it looks like they are still locked in. The Spurs are 9-2 for the season, and they have been perfect on the road. San Antonio didn't need to make moves in the offseason, already having one of the deepest and best rosters in the league. The Spurs are young, and getting to the Finals last year gave them great experience. Now they need to convert it into closing the deal.

It is hard to even imagine if there is a flaw in this Spurs roster. Victor Wembanyama is obviously the focal point of the offense and defense, but he has been surrounded by really talented players. Guys who love to play defense, and some good shooters. I suppose you could question if De'Aaron Fox is truly the correct point guard for the team. However, I think he's been a decent enough option. Their bench of Julian Champagnie, Keldon Johnson, Tobias Harris, and Luke Kornet is good enough that they could win a reasonable number of games if they were the starters.

SPURS PHENOM VICTOR WEMBANYAMA MAKES NBA HISTORY WITH FIRST CAREER DEFENSIVE PLAYER OF THE YEAR AWARD

He seems like a hard worker who could be a long-term difference-maker. The other option is Josh Giddey, and it does seem like the franchise plans to make him the leader on offense - maybe not scoring, but certainly for playmaking.

The biggest problem has been the Bulls' defense. Essentially, it is nonexistent. They are allowing almost 130 points per game. item.title: Viral plane-etiquette debate erupts after man grabs passenger's aisle seat to sit with wife
item.description: A flight passenger aboard a Frontier Airlines plane gave up his assigned aisle seat after a man took it to sit next to his wife, igniting a fierce seat swap debate.
item.content:encoded:
A Frontier Airlines passenger gave up his assigned aisle seat after another traveler took it to sit next to his wife, creating a heated debate over airplane etiquette.

The incident occurred Sunday, Nov. 8, on a flight from Atlanta to Jacksonville, Florida, as reported by travel blog "View from the Wing."

The passenger arrived at his assigned seat, 28C, to find another man sitting there next to his wife.

MAN TRIGGERS RELATIONSHIP CRISIS BY GRABBING FIRST CLASS, LEAVING WOMAN BEHIND IN COACH

Instead of moving, the man reportedly offered the passenger his middle seat, 30E, two rows back.

A flight attendant got involved but did not settle the dispute — leaving the passenger on his own to accept the middle seat, the blog said.

"I just want to get home," the passenger reportedly said.

The account was first shared by a witness on Reddit, though the post has since been deleted.

MAJOR AIRLINE ROASTS PASSENGERS WHO JUMP UP RIGHT AFTER LANDING, IGNITING FIERCE BACKLASH

Clint Henderson, New York-based managing editor at The Points Guy, told Fox News Digital his team frequently hears complaints about bad passenger behavior.

The Points Guy recently commissioned a YouGov survey of more than 2,500 U.S. adults, which found that 42% believe airplane etiquette has worsened over the past five years.

When it comes to seat swapping, 44% of respondents said it is not rude to ask another passenger to switch seats, while 34% said it is rude, according to the survey.

Henderson said asking is acceptable, but passengers should not expect someone to give up a better seat.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"If it's an even exchange, or you want to sit with your family, I think then you have every right to ask," he said. "But you also have to know ‘no’ is a full answer, and people are allowed to refuse you."

The Frontier incident led to a similar debate online.

"Trading for [a] middle seat is outrageous. Gotta upgrade if you wanna swap," one Reddit user wrote.

Others questioned why the passenger did not insist on keeping his assigned seat, while some said they understood why a tired traveler might decide an argument was just not worth it.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"There's definitely been at least one late night flight after work where I'm just way too tired to have the energy to argue," another commenter wrote.

Henderson said seat-swapping disputes have become more complicated as travelers increasingly pay extra to get specific seats.

"It's become much more fraught because a lot of passengers have paid good money for better seats in the economy cabin," he said.

If a disagreement does arise on board, Henderson advised passengers not to escalate it themselves.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Don't try to fight with passengers yourself," he said. "Don't get involved in the drama."

Instead, he recommended calling a flight attendant and allowing the crew to handle the situation.

The survey also found that 52% of Americans blame fellow passengers for poor behavior aboard planes, rather than airline companies or social media.

"I would have thought that Americans were angry at the big airline companies, but they're actually mad at their fellow passengers, and they just want common courtesy," Henderson said.

Fox News Digital reached out to Frontier Airlines for comment.

item.title: Veterans in Congress projected to decline, but Dems bringing more first-time vets by 3-to-1 margin over GOP
item.description: Democrats send roughly three times as many veteran freshmen to the 120th Congress as Republicans, even as overall veteran representation hits a low.
item.content:encoded:
The share of military veterans in Congress is projected to fall to its lowest level in decades in the incoming 120th Congress, but while overall veteran representation continues a long-term decline, the partisan composition of the freshman class marks a sharp contrast.

Democrats are bringing roughly three times as many first-time veteran members as Republicans, and they are catching up among House members overall.

Still, as America marks Veterans Day, the numbers show the institutional voice of military service in the legislative branch is heading toward its lowest watermark in modern history.

AFTER GOP'S BRUTAL MIDTERMS, ‘CHUCK NORRIS OF FLORIDA POLITICS’ TELLS PARTY TO 'GET UP AND FIGHT'

Analysis from With Honor Action and Military Times indicates veterans will hold roughly 15% of seats when the new Congress convenes in January, down from about 19% in the outgoing body and well below the 27% recorded in 2001 before the war on terror began. That comes despite a record number of veterans running in 2026, according to the analysis.

In January 2025, there were just 28 Democrats compared to 72 Republicans, according to Military Times. Among the 79 projected for the 120th Congress, the partisan gap is closing to 33 Democrats and 46 Republicans.

In addition to the massive Republican midterm losses, at least 11 Democratic veterans are projected to win House seats for the first time.

One uncalled race between Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., and her Democratic challenger, retired Navy Rear Adm. Eileen Laubacher – a former longtime Republican who switched parties in 2024 – remains in Colorado’s 4th District. Laubacher holds a roughly 3,300-vote lead with nearly all ballots counted. Some outlets have called the race for Laubacher, an outspoken critic of War Secretary Pete Hegseth.

DEMOCRATS FAR LESS LIKELY THAN REPUBLICANS TO PRIORITIZE PATRIOTISM AS KEY VALUE, POLL FINDS

Among the confirmed Democratic freshmen are former Navy Vice Adm. Nancy Lacore, D-S.C., who was removed from her post as chief of the Navy Reserve by Hegseth in August 2025.

Other Democratic veterans entering Congress as freshmen, as first reported by National Interest:

AMERICA SAW THE BLUE WAVE COMING — BUT DRASTICALLY UNDERESTIMATED THE EXTENT OF THE DEM TSUNAMI

Several of these Democrats have criticized Hegseth’s personnel decisions, promotion interventions and focus on cultural issues, with some signaling support for heightened oversight or impeachment proceedings. Lacore, the highest-ranking veteran in the new class, has said she was never given a reason for her firing and has argued that Hegseth’s leadership has damaged military readiness.

On the Republican side, four first-time veteran members are heading to Washington:

FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: 2026 MIDTERM ELECTIONS USHER IN A BLUE WAVE AS DEMOCRATS WIN CONTROL OF CONGRESS

These Republicans have generally aligned with the administration on defense priorities, including support for Hegseth.

The decline in veteran membership in Congress includes 12 Republicans defeated this year:

GOP LAWMAKER SAYS MORE QUALIFIED OFFICIALS SHOULD LEAD PENTAGON, QUESTIONS HEGSETH'S 'MORAL COMPASS'

Among the veterans who retired or did not seek re-election, it was largely Republican (11) versus Democrat (2):

HEGSETH RIPS IMPEACHMENT PUSH FROM OUTGOING REPUBLICAN AS 'FARCE, ' 'STUNT'

Three leave Congress after running for another office and losing:

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

Four Republicans and one Democrat left office early in the past Congress or died.

item.title: Woman claims hospital injected wrong drug into her spine during knee surgery, leaving her unable to walk
item.description: Linda Gilbert's lawsuit alleges Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown injected potassium phosphate instead of mepivacaine, causing incomplete paraplegia.
item.content:encoded:
A Nashville woman is seeking $150 million from Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown, alleging that a medication error during knee replacement surgery left her with a permanent spinal cord injury.

Linda Gilbert, who was 78 at the time of the incident, alleges that hospital staff injected the wrong drug into her spinal canal during the procedure.

A total of four surgery patients received potassium phosphate instead of the intended anesthetic, mepivacaine, on Aug. 14, according to an Aug. 21 statement published on the hospital system’s website.

ORGAN HARVESTING BEGAN WHILE PATIENTS STILL SHOWED ‘SIGNS OF LIFE,’ FEDERAL INVESTIGATION FINDS

The Nov. 6 complaint, which was provided to Fox News Digital by Gilbert’s attorney, alleges the injection severely injured her spinal cord and nerves, leaving her with incomplete paraplegia, severe weakness in both legs and the inability to walk, drive or live independently.

Gilbert also developed shock and respiratory failure requiring a ventilator, according to the filing. The lawsuit alleges that the patient’s injuries are permanent and says she remained in inpatient rehabilitation at a spinal cord injury center in Atlanta at the time it was filed.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Gilbert’s lawsuit claims that staff continued using syringes from the same batch after two earlier patients reported burning pain. It also alleges medication preparation and verification failures, along with delays in treatment.

The patient is seeking $50 million in compensatory damages and $100 million in punitive damages.

Potassium phosphate is used to treat low phosphorus levels and to supply phosphorus in intravenous nutrition. Its prescribing information specifies that it must be diluted and administered through a vein.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

The label warns that excessive doses or overly rapid intravenous administration can cause dangerous heart rhythms, cardiac arrest, seizures and death, according to prescribing information available on NIH’s DailyMed. Those warnings concern intravenous use, rather than injection into the spinal canal as alleged in Gilbert’s lawsuit.

In a statement published by local NBC affiliate WSMV on Nov. 9, Ascension Saint Thomas said it was aware of the complaint and was cooperating with the legal process, but could not share additional details because the case was ongoing.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"Our hearts remain with the four patients and families impacted by the recent medication error that occurred at Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown," the hospital wrote in a Sept. 11 statement on its website.

In a Sept. 16 update, the hospital said it was working with an independent quality consultant to "guide and verify the full scope of our corrective actions and process enhancements," adding that it remained "committed to learning from this and upholding the standards of patient safety, quality, and compassionate care."

About 790,000 total knee replacements are performed each year in the U.S., according to the American College of Rheumatology.

Most patients experience substantial pain relief and improved mobility, with only 2% reporting serious complications, the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons states.

Medication safety recommendations emphasize the importance of clear labeling of drugs, including their names and concentrations, and reading the label to correctly identify each medication before administration. 

Fox News Digital reached out to Ascension Saint Thomas, Gilbert’s attorney, the Tennessee Health Facilities Commission and the Institute for Safe Medication Practices for comment.

item.title: Protesters target Alex Ovechkin's Ottawa game as World Juniors Russia debate intensifies
item.description: Alex Ovechkin's game in Ottawa drew massive Ukrainian-Canadian protests over his vocal support for Vladimir Putin amid the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war.
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian-Canadian protesters came out in droves on Tuesday as Russian NHL player Alex Ovechkin played in his first game in the country this season, which will be his last in the league.

Ovechkin has been outspoken in his support for Vladimir Putin, and his game against the Ottawa Senators came weeks before the World Juniors will be held in Alberta as Russian athletes' participation remains up in the air.

"I don't know what to say," Ovechkin said of the protests before the game.

"It's absolutely not acceptable," Mike Ryndzak, a member of the Ukrainian Canadian Congress said of Ovechkin playing in Ottawa, via CBC. "It's a war. Destruction and devastation is going on as we speak and for them it's business as usual.

The UCC last month called on Canada to ban Ovechkin "and other supporters of Russia’s genocide against Ukraine."

As for the World Juniors, Canada officials originally said Russian players would be barred from playing next month despite the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) lifting the ban. The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) said it disagreed with the CAS but said last week it is "taking the necessary steps required" to comply with the CAS ruling to allow Russia to play.

Prime Minister Mark Carney originally said Russian athletes would not be permitted to play.

PUTIN ACCUSES HOCKEY ORGANIZATIONS OF 'GROSS VIOLATION' AS CANADA BARS RUSSIA FROM WORLD JUNIORS

"It’s his thoughts, his decisions," Ovechkin said of Carney.

"But I’m pretty sure if you’re going to ask the fans, the fans want to see the best players out there. And the fans want to see young generation players who are going to be future stars, future NHLers. But it’s not up to us."

Russia did not compete in Olympic hockey earlier this year, the first since 2014 that had NHL players, nor was it included in the NHL's 4 Nations Face-Off. Russia invaded Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, four days after Olympic competition ended.

Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic, Norway, Latvia and Denmark came out with statements signing up for a boycott of games against Russia as long as the war in Ukraine is ongoing. Germany, the host of the 2027 men's world championships, also suggested backing out if Russia was allowed to play.

Putin put out a statement through the state-run Russian outlet TASS calling out organizations that are preventing Russian athletes from competing for their country.

item.title: Here's what happens when someone with no experience hits an iconic racetrack in a 795-hp beast
item.description: The 795-horsepower Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC hit Sebring International Raceway, and its supercharged Predator V8 proved surprisingly approachable.
item.content:encoded:
I'm a big motorsports fan, and like cars (obviously), so a bucket list item for me was to do some track driving.

I thought that would be the usual first step — something light without too much power, like a Mazda MX-5 on a basic track — but it turns out I had an opportunity to dive right in by getting behind the wheel of a 4,100-pound, 795-horsepower beast that is the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC.

Better yet, I got to take it to the legendary, and infamously tricky, Sebring International Raceway.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Talk about jumping into the deep end in the best way.

The Mustang Dark Horse SC is the spiritual successor to the now-out-of-production Ford Shelby GT500. However, it's far from a simple rebadging.

Ford Racing developed the Dark Horse SC with a supercharged (that's where SC comes from) 5.2-liter Predator V8 engine, along with specially designed aerodynamic parts. The car starts at around $108,000, but the upgraded Track Package brings in some added performance by removing the rear seat, then adding in a Magneride damping system and carbon ceramic brakes that are the same as those used on the Ford Mustang GTD supercar.

I got to try the track package, first on an autocross course made up of cones. This was ideal, because despite the lower speeds and traction control, I still had visions of myself stepping on the loud pedal and, thanks to the 660 lb.-ft. of torque, earning me a one-way ticket to not being able to show my face within 50 miles of Sebring.

Thankfully, that didn't happen.

This car is meant to be something you can drive to the track, let loose on the track, and then drive home. That showed. It really has the DNA of a racecar, but it's perfectly suitable for daily use.

While my daily driver is a Ford Bronco Sport with a whopping 181 horsepower, the Dark Horse SC was way more approachable than I thought it would be for someone like myself who has never experienced that kind of power.

After getting through the autocross without even denting a cone (I think; if I did, the nice folks working the event were too kind to tell me), I headed to pit lane to throw on a helmet and a head-and-neck restraint to take this puppy on track.

This is where you really get a sense of what this car can do.

It was wild. We drove a few laps, and the thing that struck me first was what a full sensory experience it was.

You felt the G-forces, you felt the track (though those dampers and the car's suspension did wonders on the notoriously bumpy Sebring surface), and of course, you hear and feel that Predator V8.

I mean, the turbocharged inline-3-cylinder in my car is a fine engine. Very efficient.

But when it comes to going from that to the Predator V8 in terms of sound, volume, and sheer power, it's like going from a kazoo to a Les Paul plugged into a Marshall stack.

That said, it's still a comfortable ride. That's why it has some daily-drive pedigree. It's a beast, but not one that will rattle the fillings out of your teeth.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

What struck me most was that despite the intimidating specs, the folks at Ford insisted that this was an approachable sports car even for novices like myself, and they were right. Obviously, I didn't have the car anywhere near its limit (we left that for the pros, and the hot lap I got to take with one behind the wheel was insane), but I always felt like it was going to do exactly what I wanted. No surprises.

That's obviously what you want, and it was certainly appreciated when you have the throttle down on Sebring's backstretch. I hit 129 mph, which means there was a lot left on the table. Watching my lap back, I got on the throttle way too late before the straight. Nonetheless, when I did hit those speeds, I knew that those carbon-ceramic brakes were going to do their job of slowing me down.

And, boy, did they do it well.

I love cars, but I'm by no means an expert when it comes to sports cars. But the thing is, I think that's what impressed me most about the Mustang Dark Horse SC.

I've never driven anything like it, and yet I was able to hop behind the wheel and feel very comfortable with it in just a few minutes.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Better yet, with all the drive modes, the six levels of traction control settings, and a 7-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission, it seemed to me like an ideal sports car to get comfortable with. As you get better, just start switching modes, using those paddle shifters, and reducing the traction control.

Now, the next step is to convince my wife we need to get one of these... and I guess round up the money for it.

item.title: Dana White's Power Slap takes a swing at Lingerie Fighting Championship after debut of Power Spank
item.description: Dana White's Power Slap sent a cease and desist to the Lingerie Fighting Championships over its butt-slapping parody event called Power Spank.
item.content:encoded:
Can we live in a world where both slapping and spanking combat sports exist? I'd like to believe so. It appears that for both to live in harmony there's going to be a battle between the two organizations in court first.

The apparent upcoming court battle isn’t over the right of there to be slapping and spanking events, it reportedly has to do with the name. Power Slap, co-owned by UFC's Dana White, would like Power Spank to stop using that name.

According to MMA Junkie, a cease and desist letter was sent to the Lingerie Fighting Championships by the Power Slap attorneys after the LFC debuted Power Spank during an event in Florida last month.

The Power Spank portion of the event featured a butt-slapping competition between scantily-clad women. The LFC called Power Spank a parody that is protected speech under the First Amendment in response to the cease and desist letter.

Shaun Donnelly, the CEO of LFC, said in a statement that they won't be bullied into backing down, reports MMA Junkie:

"We respect Power Slap and its founders, but we will not be bullied into abandoning protected speech. We will defend our right, and the right of every American, to free speech, and if that takes us to the Supreme Court, we are prepared to go."

GINA CARANO SAYS DEFENDING FREE SPEECH AGAINST DISNEY WAS WORTH THE COST AHEAD OF NETFLIX FIGHT

The Power Slap parody was launched, according to Donnelly, in response to one of the LFC fighters being injured while competing.

"We watched one of our fighters get seriously hurt (at Power Slap) …" Donnelly alleged. "Power Spank is our answer: same energy, same theatrics, none of the brain damage. And let’s be honest, a spank is a lot more fun to watch than a slap."

The butt-slapping parody isn't just a gimmick. Donnelly claims that "it's a statement. Combat sports can be bold and outrageous without being reckless. Power Spank proves you can still pack a house without packing an ambulance."

item.title: Israel's political shake-up enters new phase as former PM plays kingmaker — and deadline looms
item.description: Benjamin Netanyahu called for unity, but Gadi Eisenkot canceled Likud talks after calling the outgoing prime minister's speech "delusional."
item.content:encoded:
Israel's newly elected parliament was sworn in Tuesday, marking the beginning of a political transition that could end Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's long tenure in power. Despite the opposition's parliamentary gains, the country remains without a new government, and negotiations to form one face significant obstacles.

At the center of those negotiations is former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot, who was tasked by President Isaac Herzog on Sunday with assembling Israel's next governing coalition after 67 lawmakers recommended him for the position, compared with 46 who supported Netanyahu.

Although Eisenkot's Yashar party won 21 seats in the Oct. 27 election, he is working closely with former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett, whose B'Yachad party, formed with former Prime Minister Yair Lapid, secured another 12 seats.

NETANYAHU FACES COALITION SHOWDOWN AS RIVALS MANEUVER TO FORM ISRAEL'S NEXT GOVERNMENT

The two parties have not merged, but their cooperation effectively gives Eisenkot the negotiating backing of 33 lawmakers — more than Netanyahu's Likud, which remains the largest individual party in the Knesset with 27 seats.

A source with knowledge of discussions within the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu told Fox News Digital that Bennett has decided to act as a political kingmaker, supporting Eisenkot's leadership bid rather than seeking the premiership himself.

Bennett intends to coordinate closely with Eisenkot throughout the negotiations while preserving his party's independent leadership and parliamentary identity, according to the source.

The arrangement does not create a new 33-seat party or guarantee that the two leaders will agree on every coalition arrangement. But it places Eisenkot in a stronger negotiating position than his party's 21 seats alone would suggest.

During Tuesday's swearing-in of the new Knesset, Netanyahu called for a national unity government, citing Israel's security challenges, but also sharply attacked the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government dependent on their votes.

Bennett, normally an outspoken political figure who has largely avoided the spotlight during the coalition negotiations, broke his relative silence to repeatedly confront Netanyahu during the speech.

FORMER ISRAELI PM EMERGES AS WILD CARD IN HIGH-STAKES ELECTION WITH MIDDLE EAST'S FUTURE AT STAKE

"What about your Qatari advisors?" Bennett shouted, referring to the investigation into allegations that members of Netanyahu's inner circle had financial ties to Qatar while working for the prime minister. Bennett also demanded to know why Netanyahu had not established a state commission of inquiry into the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and challenged him to declare Qatar an enemy state.

The confrontation disrupted Netanyahu's address, with other lawmakers joining the shouting as the prime minister continued warning against a government supported by Arab parties.

Eisenkot responded with an unusually forceful condemnation. "I sat and listened to the outgoing prime minister’s delusional, divisive, hate-filled and shameful speech," Eisenkot said in a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Nov. 10. "I am now even more convinced that he is unfit to remain in office for even one more minute."

Eisenkot subsequently instructed his negotiating team to cancel a meeting scheduled with Likud representatives for Wednesday.

In a separate statement, Yashar said the canceled meeting had been intended to explore coalition possibilities based on Eisenkot's four governing principles, but Netanyahu's speech made the planned discussions untenable.

FORMER ISRAELI ARMY CHIEF GADI EISENKOT EMERGES AS NETANYAHU’S LEADING ELECTION CHALLENGER

Netanyahu, however, continued advocating for a unity government on Wednesday, arguing that Israel's security challenges demanded cooperation across political divisions, according to The Times of Israel.

Despite the public confrontation, a national unity government remains one of the most tangible scenarios under consideration, according to a source with knowledge of negotiations within the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu.

The source told Fox News Digital that such an arrangement would depend on Netanyahu agreeing not to serve as prime minister first, potentially allowing Eisenkot to lead the government under a rotation agreement while Netanyahu assumes the position of alternate prime minister.

Eisenkot's allies are keeping several options open, according to the source, including agreements with ultra-Orthodox or Arab parties, partly to strengthen their negotiating position and increase pressure on Netanyahu to accept a power-sharing arrangement.

But whether Netanyahu would agree to relinquish the premiership, even temporarily, remains unclear. The source emphasized that negotiations are fluid and that no agreement has been reached.

NETANYAHU GAINS OVERNIGHT AS ISRAEL ELECTION HEADS TOWARD POLITICAL DEADLOCK

The official election results left Netanyahu's bloc with 53 seats, while the four parties seeking to replace him secured 48. The remaining 19 seats went to two Arab-led parties: the Joint List, with 11, and Ra'am, led by Mansour Abbas, with eight.

While 67 lawmakers supported Eisenkot receiving the mandate to form a government, that support does not automatically translate into a workable governing coalition.

Herzog acknowledged the challenge during consultations with parliamentary leaders, citing disagreements and mutual political vetoes that could prevent either side from forming a stable government.

Eisenkot's principal partners are Bennett, Lapid, Yair Golan of the Democrats and Avigdor Liberman of Yisrael Beytenu. Together, their parties hold 48 seats, 13 short of the 61 generally needed for a parliamentary majority.

Eisenkot has outlined four principles for potential coalition partners: recognizing Israel as a Jewish and democratic state, accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence, supporting military or civilian national service for all, and recognizing Hamas as a terrorist organization whose military and governing capabilities must be dismantled.

But those conditions have created a difficult political equation.

The ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism, collectively hold 13 seats — precisely the number Eisenkot's existing four-party bloc would need to reach 61.

However, both parties have historically opposed broadening military conscription to include ultra-Orthodox religious students, directly conflicting with Eisenkot's demand for national service.

At a Nov. 10 faction meeting, Eisenkot reiterated that he would not abandon the principle of universal military, national or civilian service, according to The Times of Israel.

The disagreement became even more visible Wednesday, when Bennett's party submitted legislation proposing expanded benefits for soldiers and reservists, while United Torah Judaism introduced bills seeking to preserve military draft exemptions for religious students, The Times of Israel reported Tuesday.

The Arab parties present a different challenge.

While Ra'am's eight lawmakers could help Eisenkot establish a government, Liberman has rejected relying on Arab parties, and the political acceptability of such an arrangement remains disputed within the bloc.

A source within Eisenkot's party told Fox News Digital that the party has not categorically ruled out cooperation with Ra'am, provided its leadership accepts the four governing principles.

The source acknowledged that negotiations remain difficult and that multiple coalition arrangements are still under consideration.

One option involves securing the support of ultra-Orthodox parties. Another would require cooperation with Arab lawmakers, potentially including support from outside the government. A broader national unity arrangement involving Likud has also been discussed.

Each scenario presents political obstacles, leaving Eisenkot facing the difficult task of assembling a coalition among parties with sharply different views on religion, national identity and security policy.

NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE

Even without a new government, Eisenkot and his allies have begun exercising their influence in the newly sworn-in parliament.

In a Monday statement provided to Fox News Digital, Yashar announced that it had submitted legislation to establish a state commission of inquiry into the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and introduce term limits for the prime minister.

The party also submitted proposals to repeal legislation associated with Netanyahu's judicial overhaul, including changes to the judiciary, the attorney general's authority, the police and the circumstances under which a prime minister can be declared unable to serve.

A vote to replace current Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana, a Netanyahu ally, is scheduled for Nov. 17.

The appointments could give Eisenkot's allies considerable influence over Israel's legislative agenda before they secure control of the government.

Beyond the domestic political negotiations, Eisenkot has also sought to reassure American leaders about the future of U.S.-Israel relations.

In a Nov. 4 public statement addressed to Americans and the international community, Eisenkot pledged to restore bipartisan cooperation with Washington and deepen Israel's relationship with the United States.

"The bond between Israel and the United States is more than an alliance between governments," Eisenkot wrote. "It is a partnership between peoples, built over generations, sustained by shared democratic values, and strengthened by the conviction that our nations are more secure and more prosperous when we stand together."

He also directly addressed his willingness to work with President Donald Trump.

"I look forward to working closely and constructively with President Trump and his administration, whose friendship and commitment to Israel we deeply value," Eisenkot said.

The message comes amid heightened debate in Washington over the future of U.S. support for Israel, following the American midterm elections and disagreements over the country's regional policies.

A source within Eisenkot's party told Fox News Digital that rebuilding relations with the United States, including with both major American political parties, would be among the priorities of a new government.

Eisenkot has also emphasized his intention to pursue regional cooperation and diplomatic opportunities while maintaining Israel's security commitments.

ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW

Under Israeli law, Eisenkot has 28 days from Nov. 8 to form a government, giving him until Dec. 6 to reach an agreement. Herzog can grant an extension of up to 14 additional days, potentially pushing the deadline to Dec. 20.

If Eisenkot fails, the president may give another lawmaker the opportunity to form a government. Additional parliamentary procedures would follow if a second attempt also fails, potentially culminating in another national election.

The outcome could determine not only who becomes Israel's next prime minister, but also the country's direction on military conscription, judicial reform, accountability for October 7 and its relations with Washington.

For now, Israel is experiencing an unusual political transition: a newly elected parliament is beginning to challenge the outgoing government's agenda, while the leader tasked with forming its replacement is still negotiating over who will join him.

Eisenkot has the presidential mandate, Bennett's backing and the support of a parliamentary majority willing to recommend him. What he does not yet have is an agreement among those parties on how to govern together.

item.title: High school recruit flips commitment from Colorado to Mississippi State back to Colorado in 30-hour span
item.description: Li'Marcus Jones, a top Nashville offensive tackle, flipped from Colorado to Mississippi State only to reverse course back to the Buffs within 30 hours.
item.content:encoded:
Stop me if you've heard this before, but college football recruiting is not for the faint of heart.

I mentioned it yesterday, but this is a 365-day-a-year racket, and if coaches don't stay on top of things in the talent acquisition world, they'll be run out of town so fast it will make your head spin.

Recruiting is the lifeblood of every great program, but unfortunately, a lot of the inner workings of acquiring high school talent is getting on a plane every weekend and telling a bunch of 16- and 17-year-olds how great they are, only to see them choose another school in the 11th hour because they offered their grandma a house or something.

It's a thankless job, and oftentimes the antics of some of these high school athletes will be enough to make you want to stop watching college football altogether.

Take Li'Marcus Jones, for example (great name, by the way).

Jones is an offensive tackle from the Nashville area and one of the top recruits in the state of Tennessee.

For a while, he was verbally committed to the University of Colorado.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL COACHING CAROUSEL COULD EXPLODE AS LINCOLN RILEY AND DEION SANDERS FACE MOUNTING PRESSURE

With how the season is going for coach Prime and the Buffs, though, it was only a matter of time before some of their committed prospects started to look elsewhere, and Jones apparently decided to finally pull the plug and stay a little closer to home, opting to flip to Mississippi State on Monday afternoon.

Seems like a solid choice, given the Bulldogs' success early in the season when quarterback Kamario Taylor and running back Fluff Bothwell were still healthy.

It is a program on the rise, especially on offense, and I'm sure any lineman would be more than happy to block for those two guys.

But just as it seemed Li'Marcus found his home for the next four years (or at least until the transfer portal opened next winter), it happened.

30 hours.

That's all it took for Jones to get cold feet and flip back to Colorado.

You would think someone would tell this kid, "Hey, take a day or two to think this over before doing something rash."

Or, at the very least, hand him a dictionary so he can look up the word "commitment."

FIVE-STAR TEXAS A&M OFFENSIVE LINE COMMIT GETS TORCHED ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR AWKWARD HAT RITUAL

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

I'm not trying to pick on Li'Marcus here, because plenty of recruits do stuff like this.

Hell, he's not even the first one to do it this recruiting cycle.

Oddly enough, this happened back in June, also involving Colorado and a school from the Magnolia State (Ole Miss).

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

You know what they say, if I had a nickel for every time a 2027 high school football recruit pulled the old "flip snip-snap" between Colorado and an SEC school from Mississippi, I'd have two nickels.

Which isn't a lot, but it's weird it happened twice.

item.title: Veterans Day 2026 brings free meals at popular restaurants — and some deals don't end Nov. 11
item.description: About 30 restaurants are offering Veterans Day deals on Nov. 11, from Outback Steakhouse's free Bloomin' Onion to Buffalo Wild Wings' boneless wings.
item.content:encoded:
Veterans and active-duty military members can find free food and other promotions at restaurants across the country on Veterans Day, Nov. 11. Some offers also give customers a reason to return for another deal later.

About 30 restaurant brands are included in Dinova's 2026 Veterans Day Dining Guide, according to Alison Quinn, the company's Florida-based president. 

The guide is in its fifth year and includes national and regional chains like Bonefish Grill, Carrabba's Italian Grill, Hooters, Outback Steakhouse and Red Lobster.

102-YEAR-OLD NAVY VETERAN STILL CRAVES HOT WINGS AFTER 102 COMBAT MISSIONS IN KOREA: 'I MIGHT MAKE IT TO 115'

"What we're starting to see now is it's going beyond Veterans Day, to try to give back to the vets in a way that is more meaningful," Quinn told Fox News Digital. "Just not about one day but come back, and we'll give you something again."

Quinn pointed to California-based Hofman Hospitality Group, which is offering select meals to veterans and a $10 bonus card for a future visit. Lucille's Smokehouse Bar-B-Que is among the group's brands.

Outback Steakhouse is offering a complimentary Bloomin' Onion and soft drink, along with a meal offer for a return visit, she said.

Other deals listed in the guide include 10 free boneless wings and fries at Buffalo Wild Wings, a complimentary Red's Big Tavern Burger at Red Robin, free shrimp at Red Lobster and a free All-American Smash at Smashburger.

Dinova started the guide to share offers with veterans and, in some cases, active-duty military personnel, Quinn said. The company's business dining network includes about 25,000 restaurants and 600 corporate partners, she said.

Downloads of the guide have increased over the years, Quinn said, and the promotions may be useful for veterans or active-duty personnel who are struggling or "living under a tight budget."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Asked which deal she would choose, Quinn singled out Eddie Merlot's complimentary cheeseburger. Her father is an 85-year-old veteran, she said, and she plans to tell him about it.

Veterans and active-duty military members should bring identification and check with their local restaurant before visiting, Quinn said. Participation and ID requirements can vary by location and offer.

item.title: Browns confirm no quarterback controversy as Deshaun Watson reclaims starting job over Shedeur Sanders
item.description: Deshaun Watson will reclaim his starting role for the Cleveland Browns despite Shedeur Sanders' near-overtime heroics against the New Orleans Saints.
item.content:encoded:
There appears to be no quarterback controversy for the Cleveland Browns.

Shedeur Sanders was just one completion away from giving the Browns a wild overtime win over the New Orleans Saints this past weekend, as Deshaun Watson missed the Week 9 contest.

However, Watson will recapture his spot as the team's starting quarterback on Sunday.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Watson entered concussion protocol last week and was actually cleared ahead of the game against the Saints, but the Browns rocked with Sanders anyway.

The Colorado alum had impressive numbers, going 19-for-31 for 297 passing yards and two touchdowns - a 64-yard score to KC Concepcion in the fourth quarter and a 39-yard catch-and-run to Harold Fannin Jr. in overtime.

Cleveland went for a two-point conversion and the win, but the New Orleans pass rush immediately pressured Sanders. He scrambled to his right before throwing an incomplete pass intended for Denzel Boston, ending the game.

Watson is in the final year of his dreaded five-year, $230 million contract that the Browns have all but admitted to regretting. Sanders, once thought of as a top-five pick, fell to the fifth round of last year's NFL Draft and entered the season as the third-string quarterback behind Joe Flacco and fellow rookie Dillon Gabriel.

TOM BRADY ADMITS TO MORE MOTIVATION AFTER DEFLATEGATE SUSPENSION, REVEALS WHAT HE DID WHILE AWAY FROM PATRIOTS

Flacco was traded, and Gabriel suffered a concussion, bringing Sanders into the fold, but when he won his first NFL start, he was the starter for the remainder of the season.

Watson, however, returned from a torn Achilles, and it never quite seemed like his job as a starter was in doubt, as long as he was healthy.

In his eight games - his most since 2020 - Watson has completed 65.5% of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions.

Sanders is 3-5 as a starter - he threw for 1,400 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 picks in his eight games last year (seven starts).

OutKick's Dan Zaksheske contributed to this report.

item.title: Antonio Sabato Jr and Virginia Madsen's son arrested in fatal hit-and-run
item.description: Jack Sabato, son of Antonio Sabato Jr. and Virginia Madsen, faces felony charges after a fatal hit-and-run in Anchorage, Alaska, police say.
item.content:encoded:
Antonio Sabato Jr. and Virginia Madsen’s son, Jack Sabato, has been arrested in connection with a fatal hit-and-run in Anchorage, Alaska, Fox News Digital has confirmed.

According to the Anchorage Police Department, Sabato, 32, was arrested Nov. 9 on charges of leaving the scene of an accident without assisting the injured and leaving the scene of an accident resulting in injury or death.

Police identified the victim as Carl Simmonds, 42, who was pronounced dead after officers and medics responded to reports of an unresponsive man near Airport Heights Drive and Debarr Road around 5:48 a.m. A preliminary investigation indicated a vehicle struck Simmonds and fled the scene, police said.

VIRGINIA MADSEN SAYS VETERANS AREN'T TRAINED TO COME HOME AFTER NEPHEW'S SUICIDE

According to court records obtained by Fox News Digital, Jack has been hit with a felony charge of leaving the scene of an accident without helping the victim, as well as a misdemeanor charge of leaving the scene of an accident involving injury or death.

Charging documents reviewed by Alaska Public Media reported that responding officers found Simmonds' body on the sidewalk off Airport Heights Drive and several car parts scattered around.

While reviewing security footage from a nearby bank, officers saw a white Chevy Tahoe striking Simmonds and not braking before or after the crash, according to the outlet.

After running the vehicle’s description into the Alaska Public Safety Information Network, law enforcement found the matching vehicle — which is registered to Jack — parked at the Anchorage Amazon warehouse. The vehicle was then seized.

According to the charging documents, Jack told police he struck "something" while driving home after delivering for DoorDash, damaging his headlights. "Thank you."
